text:
Elena W: quick heads-up 10: I noticed our Troubleshooting page still references the old timeout examples that talk about `client.timeout_ms` which we removed in the SDK v2 migration.
Ravi D: ugh, good catch. which file?
Elena W: `docs/troubleshooting/errors.md` under 'timeouts' and the JS snippet in '429 handling' both use it. linked from a customer support thread too.
Marta S: thanks. we should do two things: 1) update snippets to the new `sdk.configure({ timeout: { request: ms } })` API, 2) add a migration note explaining the rename.
doc-bot: opened issue #476 in docs repo: "migrate timeout and retry snippets to SDK v2"
Elena W: I'll take the migration note paragraph. can someone update the JS + Python examples?
Ravi D: I'll update JS. quick draft plan: - replace `client.timeout_ms` usages - add snippet showing check for `X-RateLimit-Reset` and fallback loop - illustrate fallback to a lower-cost model when remaining tokens < 100. keep examples minimal.
Marta S: small UX item: add a note about when to prefer immediate model switch vs exponential backoff. customers with interactive chat tend to prefer switch, batch jobs prefer backoff.
Elena W: yep add a one-line guidance and link to rollout/capacity docs for Dedicated.
Ravi D: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2367 10 title: "migrate timeout/retry snippets to SDK v2 + 429 example"
doc-bot: automated lint check: snippet lint failed on one Python code fence (missing import).
Ravi D: fixing now. also adding `sdk.metrics.increment('fallback_triggered')` in the examples to encourage telemetry.
Marta S: small nit in PR: change wording from "switch to smaller model" to "fallback to a lower-cost model variant". keeps it consistent with our policy doc.
Ravi D: updated wording. pushed.
Elena W: I added the migration note and a short subsection "SDK v1 -> v2: timeouts & retries" with before/after snippet. also added a link to the SDK changelog.
Infra QA: QA note 0: please include a reproducible command for our sandbox: `make sandbox-e2e && ./tools/simulate_rate_limit --model=gpt-4-small --limit=1` that triggers 429s for testing the snippet.
doc-bot: CI passed for docs build. requesting reviews: @Marta S, @Elena W.
Marta S: left 2 comments: one to add a table row in the error matrix mapping header signals to actions, and another to ensure the code sample uses the SDK's `retry.delay(ms)` instead of raw `setTimeout`.
Ravi D: replaced setTimeout with `await sdk.retry.delay(ms)` in JS. added the header-action table.
Elena W: approving after QA checklist addition. can we also add a tiny redirect for the old anchor `/docs/errors#timeouts-v1` to `/docs/troubleshooting/timeouts`? some customers bookmarked it.
Marta S: I'll drop a short Netlify redirect in the infra site config.
doc-bot: PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2367 11 deployed to staging.

Elena W: deployed to staging and validated that: - migration note renders - all old `client.timeout_ms` occurrences are gone - JS and Python snippets show v2 usage - reproduction command in QA checklist works.
Infra QA: ran sandbox test, simulated repeated 429s. logs show `fallback_reason=rate_limit` and telemetry event `fallback_triggered` recorded.
Marta S: nice. follow-up: open a tiny test that fails CI if the runbook contains `client.timeout_ms` (simple grep in docs CI).
Elena W: opened issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/489 "CI check to catch legacy SDK timeout keys"
Ravi D: added a short note in the SDK migration guide linking back to the runbook.
Elena W: thanks all. closing this thread.
